## R Markdown & Brief Intro.

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

** What is R Markdown? **

R Markdown is a file format that allows you to turn your data analysis into high-quality documents, reports, and presentations. It is built on Literate Programming, a concept where the explanation (narrative text) and the machine code (R chunks) exist in the same document.


## Narrative 

Transitioning from running scripts in RStudio to authoring in R Markdown provides a more integrated workflow for data analysis. While I am accustomed to using Base R for granular control over my data frames and visualizations, the Markdown environment allows me to document the "why" behind my code as I write it. This process ensures that my logic remains transparent, making it easier to revisit my analysis later or share it with others without needing to explain every step manually.



## LaTeX Math Expression

## 2 R Code Chunks

Chunk 1:
{r cars}
* Load the built-in cars dataset *
data(cars)

* Display the first few rows and summary statistics *
head(cars)
summary(cars)

Chunk 2:
{r ggplot2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
* Load the ggplot2 library *
library(ggplot2)

* Create a scatter plot with a regression line *
ggplot(cars, aes(x = speed, y = dist)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "darkred") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Speed vs. Stopping Distance",
       x = "Speed (mph)",
       y = "Stopping Distance (ft)")
